claims.claim: Pydantic v2 validation with effective extra="forbid" rejects input fields not declared by the model.

newer_practice.summary: Pydantic 2.12 introduced per-validation extra overrides. This reinforces the claim's qualification that extra='forbid' must be effective for the validation call; no step change is required.

claims.recommended_action: No change required. Retain the qualification 'effective' because validation-call overrides can replace model configuration.

sources.quote: 'forbid': Providing extra data is not permitted
sources.title: Configuration | Pydantic Docs

claims.claim: Pydantic 2.13.5 model_copy(update=...) applies updates without validating the supplied values.

newer_practice.summary: The 2.14.0a1 prerelease changes deep copying to exclude fields replaced by updates. This related development does not supersede the verified behavior of version 2.13.5 or require adopting the prerelease.

claims.recommended_action: No change required. Preserve the explicit distinction between copying with updates and validating those updates.

sources.quote: Note: the data is not validated before creating the new model.
sources.title: Pydantic v2.13.5 source: BaseModel.model_copy

claims.claim: SQLite permits one simultaneous write transaction per database, and BEGIN IMMEDIATE can fail with SQLITE_BUSY when another connection already has an active write transaction.

newer_practice.summary: SQLite 3.50.0 added sqlite3_setlk_timeout(), a separate timeout for builds supporting blocking locks. This adds lock-wait configuration without replacing the single-writer rule or eliminating possible SQLITE_BUSY results; no step change is established.

claims.recommended_action: No change required. Retain both the single-writer constraint and the possibility of SQLITE_BUSY when beginning a competing write transaction.

sources.quote: one simultaneous write transaction. … BEGIN IMMEDIATE might fail with SQLITE_BUSY
sources.title: Transaction — SQLite

claims.claim: Executing RAISE(ABORT, message) in a SQLite trigger terminates the current query and returns SQLITE_CONSTRAINT with the supplied message.
claims.recommended_action: No change required. The official trigger documentation directly supports the stated termination and error behavior; no relevant superseding practice was found in the search window.

sources.quote: RAISE(ABORT,...) … query terminates. … SQLITE_CONSTRAINT … specified error message.
sources.title: CREATE TRIGGER — SQLite, section 6: The RAISE() function

claims.claim: Python 3.12 hashlib provides sha256, and a hash object's hexdigest method returns its digest as hexadecimal text.
claims.recommended_action: No change required. Keep the version-specific API statement; no relevant replacement for sha256 or hexdigest was found in the search window.

sources.quote: sha256() … returned as a string object … containing only hexadecimal digits.
sources.title: hashlib — Secure hashes and message digests — Python 3.12 documentation

claims.claim: RFC 8785 sorts JSON object property names using unsigned UTF-16 code units and encodes the resulting canonical serialization in UTF-8.

newer_practice.summary: The dated Canonical Payload Binding Internet-Draft uses RFC 8785 JCS without an added normalization pass. This is related work in progress, not a replacement for RFC 8785; it requires no change to this step.

claims.recommended_action: No change required. Retain unsigned UTF-16 ordering and UTF-8 output. This finding verifies the specification statement, not implementation conformance.

sources.quote: UTF-16 … code units. … unsigned integers … encoded in UTF-8.
sources.title: RFC 8785: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS), sections 3.2.3–3.2.4
